title: PSRC method Included in Singapore Building Design Standard
body:
The PSRC (Prefabricated SRC) column method has been included as an independent chapter in BC4:2025, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA)'s design guide for high-strength steel-concrete composite columns.

BC4:2025 is the basic design guide for all buildings constructed in Singapore and covers design methods for composite columns using high-strength steel and concrete, based on Eurocode 4.

The Building and Construction Authority (BCA), noting the safety, economic viability and innovation of the method through several projects constructed using PSRC in Singapore, established an entirely new Chapter 6 for the specific method. It also included a range of examples applying PSRC in Example Calculations to the Requirement of BC4:2025.

As one of the leaders in OSC (Off-Site Construction), which is gaining attention as the construction industry's next major focus, PSRC is being widely applied to semiconductor plants, data centers and advanced manufacturing facilities, where demand has grown in the AI (artificial intelligence) era. In Singapore, it has been applied at Hyundai Motor Group Innovation Center Singapore (HMGICS) and JTC Logistics Hub. JTC Logistics Hub, in particular, was selected as BCA Project of the Year 2024 (Industrial Buildings category).

Singapore maintains some of the world's strictest construction and structural safety standards while actively embracing technological innovation, giving it significant influence over nearby Southeast Asia construction markets. This achievement is expected to significantly strengthen the credibility of the PSRC method not only in Southeast Asia, including Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, but also in other overseas markets.
